Words used in the present tense shall include the future, the word "shall" is mandatory and not directory, the word "person" includes a firm, organization, partnership, trust or corporation, and the word "city" shall mean the City of Stone Mountain, Georgia.
Abandoned sign shall mean a sign that exists when the business activity or firm which such sign advertises is no longer in operation, has moved from the registered business address, or does not have a current occupational tax certificate.
Animated sign shall mean a sign that all or any part thereof visibly moves or uses movement or a change of lighting to depict action or to create a special effect or scene. This includes signs that rotate or revolve to display a message in more than one (1) direction.
Area of a sign/sign area shall mean the total area upon which a message is displayed on any sign consisting of the smallest square, rectangle, triangle, circle, or combination thereof, which encompasses the entire sign, inclusive of any border and trim, but excluding the base, apron, supports, and other structural members.
Announcement sign shall mean a sign used to announce entrance or exit information, business hours, menus offered, off-street parking or similar information. This definition does not include advertisements.
Awning shall mean a shelter projecting from and supported by the exterior wall of a building constructed of non-rigid materials on a supporting framework,
Banner shall mean a piece of fabric or similar material which is permanently or temporarily attached to a pole, enclosed in a frame, or mounted to allow movement caused by the atmosphere.
Canopy sign shall mean a sign affixed to, superimposed upon, or painted on any roof or roof-like structure which is extended over a sidewalk, walkway or vehicle access area.
Commercial message means sign copy which identifies, advertises, or directs attention to a business, or is intended to include the purchase of goods, property, or service, including without limitation, any sign copy naming a brand of goods or service or otherwise proposing a commercial transaction.
Electronic sign shall mean a sign whose message may be changed at intervals by electronic process or by remote control, including the device known as a commercial electronic variable message sign.
Facade shall mean the exterior wall of a building facing any street which provides direct ingress and egress to the lot.
Freestanding or ground sign shall mean any sign supported by uprights or braces or resting upon a foundation in the ground that is not supported or suspended from any building, or any sign securely affixed to a substantial support structure which is permanently attached to the ground and wholly independent of any building for support.
Illegal sign shall mean any sign that was erected in violation of the law, as they existed at the time the sign permit was issued, signs that were not built in conformance with the issued permit, or signs installed without a permit unless otherwise authorized by this chapter.
Internally illuminated sign shall mean a sign that has light cast through the sign face from an internal light source.
Lot shall mean a designated parcel, tract, or area of land legally established by plat, subdivision, or as otherwise permitted by law, to be separately owned, used, developed, or built upon.
Political campaign sign means any temporary sign or other graphic erected during an election or initiative/referendum campaign to publicize candidates running for office or ballot issues.
Portable sign shall mean any sign which is manifestly designed to be transported, including by trailer or in the bed of a pick up truck or on its own wheels, even though the wheels of such sign may be removed and the remaining chassis or support constructed without wheels is converted to an "A" or "T" frame sign or attached temporarily or permanently to the ground.
Public service sign means a temporary, noncommercial sign devoted to religious, charitable, cultural, governmental or educational purposes.
Sign shall mean a device, structure or representation for visual communication which is used for the purpose of bringing the subject thereof to the attention of others. Substantial damage means damage exceeding fifty (50) percent of the value of the sign and/or sign structure at the time of destruction.
Temporary sign means a temporary sign explicitly authorized by this chapter for a period not to exceed thirty (30) days.

Wall sign shall mean a sign fastened, placed, or painted upon or parallel to the exterior wall of a structure itself, whether front, rear, or side of the structure.

(e) On multi-tenant buildings the owner must submit an overall sign program for the entire building prior to the issuance of a permit for any facade or wall sign.
(Ord. No. 2011-10, 10-4-11; Ord. No. 2020-09, § 1(Exh. A), 8-4-20)
1214:
Window/door advertising signs are allowed only in nonresidential zoning districts. Temporary window signs may be installed without a permit, but they must be installed in accordance with the provisions set forth in this section. Window advertising signs may be intended for either advertising purposes or for information purposes.
A window advertising sign is intended to promote the goods and services offered for sale at the business premises on which the sign is located. For purposes of administering this chapter, window advertising signs shall include public service signs and political campaign signs.
Such signs must be placed inside and may be taped to the window/door or frame, or may be otherwise attached or placed in the window area in order to display a message.
No more than fifty (50) percent of the windows/doors of a business premises shall be used to display window advertising signs.
No sign shall exceed more than fifty (50) percent of the pane(s) on which it is erected. Area of the pane shall be the area which encloses the individual pane. Each individual pane is considered an area of which not to exceed more than fifty (50) percent in signage. However for the purpose of this chapter any framed window area consisting of a single window pane that is divided by grids or muntins creating the appearance of smaller panes or a larger framed window area filled with smaller panes separated by muntins the total framed area shall be considered a single pane in the calculation of the fifty (50) percent coverage.
(Ord. No. 2011-10, 10-4-11)
1217:
(a) Temporary business signs. Businesses which have submitted a complete application for a permanent sign in accordance with article IV for a sign which identifies the business may be issued a permit for a temporary sign to identify the business. Such temporary business signs shall conform to the following:
(1) Only one (1) sign per premises with no more than two (2) sign faces. Any single sign face not to exceed sixteen (16) square feet.
(b) Tax exempt organization temporary signs. Tax exempt organizations conducting a fund raising event within the limits of the city may be issued a permit for a temporary sign to identify the event. Such tax exempt organization temporary signs shall conform to the following:
(1) Only one sign per premises with no more than two (2) sign faces. Any single sign face not to exceed sixteen (16) square feet.
(2) Sign to be constructed of one-half-inch duroply, or a material of equal durability, mounted on four (4) by four (4) wood posts or other sign supports to achieve the same rigidity.
(3) The signs must be placed on the premises of the event with no portion of the sign in any right-of-way or easement.
(4) Tax exempt organization temporary signs shall not be illuminated.
(c) Temporary message boards. Businesses which have a permitted permanent sign in accordance with these regulations may be issued a permit for a temporary message board sign on public property conforming to the following:
(1) Only one (1) sign per premises with no more than two (2) sign faces. Any single sign face not to exceed sixteen (16) square feet.
(2) Sign to be constructed of one-half-inch duroply, or a material of equal durability, mounted on four (4) by four (4) wood posts or other sign supports to achieve the same rigidity.
(3) Signs are to be displayed only during hours that the business is open to the public.
(4) Signs shall not be placed to block or restrict the passageway on public property to less than five (5) feet in width or block the ingress/egress to any building.
(Ord. No. 2011-10, 10-4-11; Ord. No. 2015-10, Pt. I, 9-1-15)
1218:
(a) Real estate signs or project signs not meeting the requirements of section 23-32 shall conform to the requirements of this section.
(b) The total area of a free standing real estate or project sign shall not exceed forty (40) square feet and twenty (20) square feet per sign face. The maximum height for a free standing real estate or project sign shall not exceed five (5) feet above the average grade within a twenty-foot radius of the sign and the lower edge shall not exceed four (4) feet in height from the lowest grade at the base of the sign.
(c) Real estate signs offering tenant space at a commercial center shall not be free standing but may be placed as a tenant panel on a permitted directory sign on the facade of the tenant space being offered.
(d) The total area of a facade real estate or project sign shall not exceed twenty (20) square feet.
(e) The number of real estate or project signs placed on any one premises shall be limited to:
(1) One (1) real estate sign per street frontage inclusive of those allowed by section 23-32. This sign may be double faced provided the faces are not separated by more than fifteen (15) inches.
(2) One (1) project sign inclusive of those allowed by section 23-32.
(f) Real estate or project signs shall not be illuminated.
(Ord. No. 2011-10, 10-4-11)
1219:
(a) Special event signs may be erected only with approval of the city council.
(b) Special event signs may announce only events that are sponsored by a public entity or a tax-exempt organization.
(Ord. No. 2011-10, 10-4-11)
1220:
If visible from any street right-of-way the number, location and area of directory signs shall be within the limits established by section 23-43.
(Ord. No. 2011-10, 10-4-11)
1221:
(a) Petroleum product pumps and dispensers which are within view of a public way shall be permitted to display only information required by law, the brand name and type of product being dispensed, and one (1) additional sign mounted on the pump or dispenser not to exceed one (1) square foot in size. Canopy signs are not allowed.
(b) Premises from which retail petroleum products are dispensed by pump shall be permitted one (1) additional sign with a maximum area of ten (10) square feet announcing the price per gallon of the products. In lieu of the one (1) additional sign permitted above, the price per gallon may be:
(1) Displayed on each individual pump structure with characters not exceeding six (6) inches in height; or
(2) Displayed by increasing by ten (10) square feet the area allowed by section 23-42 for a single free-standing sign.
(Ord. No. 2011-10, 10-4-11)
1222:
(a) The official flags of the federal, state, county, or municipal governments are not deemed to be signs, provided that no such flag shall exceed forty (40) square feet per face and is kept in good condition.
(b) All banner flags not exceeding ten (10) square feet per face are not deemed to be signs provided that no more than two (2) flags per premises are displayed at any one (1) time.
(Ord. No. 2011-10, 10-4-11)
1223:
(a) No more than one (1) sign per street frontage of any premises shall contain changeable copy.
(b) The area of changeable copy shall not exceed twenty (20) square feet per sign face. Copy height shall be eight (8) inches maximum and four (4) inches minimum.
(c) Changeable copy shall be limited to announcing:
(1) Motion pictures or entertainment at a theater whose primary function is to provide musical or dramatic events; or
(2) Gasoline prices as described in section 23-55.
(3) Other notices or information items.
(d) Changeable copy shall be securely fastened to the sign face and neatly maintained to appear as initially designed and placed.
(e) Special event signs as described in section 23-53 are exempt from the requirements of this section.
(Ord. No. 2011-10, 10-4-11)
1224:
All signs in publicly owned parks shall comply with the provisions of this chapter except as follows:
(1) Temporary signs are allowed at facilities rented by the public for a private event (family reunion, picnic, or similar events of non-commercial nature.) Such signs are allowed only for the period of the event.
(2) Temporary advertising signs as part of a fund raising event conducted by a youth association. Such signs can only be displayed during the regular sports season(s).
(Ord. No. 2011-10, 10-4-11)
1225:
For businesses with permitted permanent signage, banners and streamers are allowed on a temporary basis, not to exceed thirty (30) days unless otherwise extended by city council. For the purpose of this chapter a banner or streamer is a temporary flag, bunting or other flexible sign characteristically hung on a building, or otherwise suspended down or along its face intended to display a message of temporary significance. No more than one (1) banner, not to exceed sixteen (16) square feet, can be displayed at any one (1) time and not more than four (4) banners per business at one (1) location in a twelve-month period. Streamers shall not be displayed for more than thirty (30) days and not more than twice per year for the same business at the same location.
(Ord. No. 2011-10, 10-4-11)
1226:
Signs located on the fabric covering of outdoor umbrellas shall be limited to not more than twenty-five (25) percent of the total umbrella panel area. For the purpose of calculation a panel will be the fabric area between two (2) umbrella ribs. The sign area shall be considered all graphics, art work, lettering, and all other designs adjacent to or surrounding the graphics, art work, lettering. For example: an umbrella with eight (8) panels could have signs/graphics on each of the panels but the total area on each panel of the sign/graphic could not exceed twenty-five (25) percent of the panel area. However, this twenty-five (25) percent panel coverage limit may be combined. For example an umbrella with eight (8) panels could have signs/graphics on four (4) of the individual panels covering fifty (50) percent of each of those four (4) panels with the remaining four (4) panels being blank. For the purpose of this chapter graphics or letters on the fringe of the umbrella not over three (3) inches in height shall not be considered signs.
(Ord. No. 2011-10, 10-4-11)
1227:
Signs located on the fabric covering of an awning shall be limited to not more than fifty (50) percent of the total area of the canopy top of the awning. For the purpose of calculation, the total area of the canopy top of the awning shall not include the valance or the fabric covering on the sides of the awning. The sign area shall be considered all graphics, artwork, lettering, and all other designs adjacent to or surrounding the graphics, artwork, lettering. For the purposes of this chapter graphics or letters on the valance of the awning not over three (3) inches in height shall not be considered signs.
(Ord. No. 2020-09, § 1(Exh. A), 8-4-20)
1230:
The city clerk or their designee shall administer the provisions of this chapter.
(Ord. No. 2011-10, 10-4-11)
1232:
(a) A non-refundable application fee shall be paid at the time of application submission.
(b) When re-inspection is required by section 23-76 a re-inspection fee shall be charged to and paid by the subject property owner or applicant.
(c) An additional fee shall be imposed against the subject property owner or applicant for each sign or sign structure installed prior to receiving approval. This fee shall be in addition to any penalties described in article VIII.
(d) The amount of the fees imposed hereunder shall be set by resolution of the city council.
(Ord. No. 2011-10, 10-4-11; Amd. 12-5-23; Ord. No. 2024-02, § 1(Exh. A), 1-16-24)
1233:
Upon compliance with the provisions of this article, the city clerk or their designee shall make a decision to issue, deny or issue with conditions a permit for such sign within thirty (30) days of receipt of a complete permit application.
(Ord. No. 2011-10, 10-4-11)
1234:
A sign permit shall be valid for a period of ninety (90) days from the date of its issuance as noted on the permit. Failure to notify the city clerk or their designee that the sign and all items required by the permit have been completed within such ninety-day period shall result in the expiration of such permit and a new sign permit application must be submitted with the appropriate application fee.
(Ord. No. 2011-10, 10-4-11)
1235:
(a) Upon notification that the sign is complete, the city shall conduct an inspection for the purpose of verifying that the sign is in compliance with the requirements of the permit and all other provisions of this article at which time the city shall issue a final notice of compliance.
(b) Prior to the inspection of free standing signs the permittee or sign contractor shall locate and identify on the site all property lines adjacent to the sign for the purpose of verifying the sign location in relationship to such property lines.
(c) If the sign fails to pass the required inspection, the applicant shall correct any items not in compliance within ten (10) calendar days or the permit shall be deemed invalid and the sign and any sign structure shall be impounded pursuant to section 23-83.
(Ord. No. 2011-10, 10-4-11)
1238:
The city clerk or their designee shall have the authority to enter upon the premises subject to this article for the purpose of enforcing the provisions of this article.
(Ord. No. 2011-10, 10-4-11)
1239:
When a sign requiring a permit under article IV of this chapter is erected, relocated, or altered without a sign permit, the city clerk or their designee shall hand-deliver, fax or mail the notice (to the address stated on the business license) to its owner, agent or business representative indicating that they must correct the violation within five (5) calendar days of the hand delivered or faxed notice or seven (7) calendar days of the mailed notice or be subject to the enforcement action of sections 23-83 and 23-84.
(Ord. No. 2011-10, 10-4-11)
1240:
(a) The city shall have the authority to remove and hold any sign or sign structure subject to impoundment by the provisions of this article.
(b) The city shall have the authority to remove any prohibited sign without notice.
(c) The owner of an impounded sign or sign structure may recover same upon the payment of fifty dollars ($50.00) for each sign plus the costs of removal. In the event it is not claimed within ten (10) days from the date of impoundment, the city clerk shall have authority to dispose of such sign or sign structure without compensation to the owner.
(Ord. No. 2011-10, 10-4-11)
1241:
Violation of any provision of this article is subject to the penalty provisions of Code of Ordinances, City of The City of Stone Mountain. Each day's continued violation shall constitute a separate offense.
(Ord. No. 2011-10, 10-4-11)
1244:
Any aggrieved person, sign owner, applicant, or any officer, department, board or bureau of the municipality who alleges that the city acted erroneously in enforcing this article may appeal the decision of the city. Such appeal shall be filed with the city clerk within ten (10) working days of the receipt of the decision or determination. The appeal shall be reviewed by a committee consisting of the city clerk, code enforcement officer and the city attorney. The decision of this committee shall be rendered within thirty (30) calendar days from date of filing and shall be final.
(Ord. No. 2011-10, 10-4-11)
1245:
Recognizing that the strict application of the requirements of this article may work an undue hardship on certain applicants, variances from the strict application of the design and performance provisions of this chapter may be granted by the city council. Each application for a variance under this section shall be in accordance with the variance procedures as contained in the city's zoning ordinance.
(Ord. No. 2011-10, 10-4-11)
1248:
The standards and provisions of this chapter shall be interpreted as being the minimum requirements necessary to uphold the purposes of this chapter.
(Ord. No. 2011-10, 10-4-11)
1249:
Whenever this chapter imposes a more restrictive standard than required by any other city ordinance or requirement, the provisions of this chapter shall govern. Whenever any other city ordinance or requirement imposes a more restrictive standard than required by this chapter, the provisions of such city ordinance or requirement shall govern.
(Ord. No. 2011-10, 10-4-11)
1250:

1260:
The City of Stone Mountain (the "city") is vitally concerned with the use, construction within, and occupancy of all rights-of-way in the city as such rights-of-way are a valuable and limited resource which must be utilized to promote the public health, safety, welfare, economic development of the city and to protect public work infrastructure. Therefore, the city, under the authority of the Laws and Constitution of the State of Georgia, including, but not limited to, Article 9, Section 1, paragraphs 2 and 3 of the Georgia Constitution, O.C.G.A. 36-35-3 and O.C.G.A. 32-4-92(10), has adopted this article for the purpose of regulating public and private entities which use the city rights-of-way.
(Ord. No. 2015-15, Pt. I(§ 25.3), 6-2-15)
1261:
The provisions of this article shall apply to all utilities and facilities occupying the rights-of-way as provided herein.
(Ord. No. 2015-15, Pt. I(§ 25.4), 6-2-15)
1263:
Each utility who occupies, uses or has facilities in the rights-of-way at the time of passage of this article, including by lease, sublease or assignment, to operate facilities located in the rights-of-way, unless specifically exempted by state or federal law or this Code, shall file a registration statement with the director within ninety (90) days of the effective date of this article.
(Ord. No. 2015-15, Pt. I(§ 25.6), 6-2-15)
1265:
If a registration is incomplete, the director shall notify the registrant and shall provide a reasonable period of time in which to complete the registration. If a registration is complete, the director shall so notify the utility in writing.
(Ord. No. 2015-15, Pt. I(§ 25.8), 6-2-15)
1266:
Acceptance of the registration shall not convey title in the rights-of-way. Acceptance of the registration is only the nonexclusive, limited right to occupy rights-of-way in the city for the limited purposes stated in the acceptance. Acceptance of the registration does not excuse a utility from obtaining permits required by city ordinances nor from obtaining appropriate access or pole attachment agreements before using the facilities of others, including the city. Acceptance of the registration does not excuse a utility from notifying the city of construction as required herein.
(Ord. No. 2015-15, Pt. I(§ 25.9), 6-2-15)
1267:
Beginning one (1) year after the effective date of this article, any facilities or part of a facility found in a right-of-way for which registration is required but has not been obtained unless specifically exempted by law, and for which no valid service agreement exists with the city, may be deemed to be a nuisance and an unauthorized use of the rights-of-way. The city may exercise any remedies or rights it has at law or in equity, including, but not limited to abating the nuisance; taking possession of the facilities, evicting the utility from the right-of-way; prosecuting the violator; and/or any other remedy provided by city ordinance or otherwise allowed in law or in equity.
(Ord. No. 2015-15, Pt. I(§ 25.10), 6-2-15)
1268:
It shall be unlawful for any utility to excavate, or to construct, install, maintain, renew, remove or relocate facilities in, on, along, over or under the public roads of the city without a utility permit issued in accordance with the terms of this article.
(Ord. No. 2015-15, Pt. I(§ 25.11), 6-2-15)
1270:
Fees shall be determined by the director, subject to the approval by resolution of the city council. A fee schedule shall be available at the offices of the director and the city clerk and open for public inspection.
(Ord. No. 2015-15, Pt. I(§ 25.13), 6-2-15)
1271:
If the director determines the applicant has satisfied the following requirements, the director may issue a permit.
(1) Whether issuance of the permit will be consistent with this article;
(2) Whether applicant has submitted a complete application and has secured all certificates and other authorizations required by law, if applicable, in order to construct facilities in the manner proposed by the applicant; and
(3) The impact on safety, visual quality of the streets, traffic flow, and other users of the right-of-way and the difficulty and length of time of the project, construction or maintenance.
(Ord. No. 2015-15, Pt. I(§ 25.14), 6-2-15)
1272:
(1) Each utility shall, as soon as reasonably practicable, notify the director of any event regarding its facilities which it considers to be an emergency. The utility may proceed to take whatever actions are necessary in order to respond to the emergency. A utility who engages in an emergency excavation shall take all reasonable precautions to avoid or minimize damage to any existing facilities.
(2) In the event the city becomes aware of an emergency regarding utility facilities, the city may attempt to contact the affected utility or facilities representative. The city may take whatever action it deems necessary in order to respond to the emergency, including cut or move any of the wires, cables, amplifiers, appliances, or other parts of the facilities. The city shall not incur any liability to the utility, for such emergency actions, and the cost of such shall be paid by each utility affected by the emergency.
(Ord. No. 2015-15, Pt. I(§ 25.15), 6-2-15)
1274:
If the director decides there is reason or cause to revoke a permit then the city may exercise any remedies or rights it has at law or in equity to revoke the permit. The following procedure shall be followed:
(1) The city shall serve a utility with a written notice of the reason or cause for the proposed revocation and a period of time to cure the reason or cause for the proposed revocation. The period of time shall be no less than fifteen (15) calendar days from the date the notice is received by the utility; and
(2) If the utility fails to cure the reason or cause within the time period allowed in the notice, the city may revoke the permit and issue a stop work order to the utility.
(Ord. No. 2015-15, Pt. I(§ 25.17), 6-2-15)
1275:
If work is not begun within six (6) months of the date of issuance, the permit will automatically expire.
(Ord. No. 2015-15, Pt. I(§ 25.18), 6-2-15)
1276:
The 1988 Utility Accommodation Policy and Standards manual, including all references contained therein to codes, rules, regulations, schedules, forms and appendix items, except appendix B (permit forms and supporting documents), promulgated by the State of Georgia Department of Transportation, as may be amended from time to time is hereby adopted by reference and incorporated in the article as if fully set forth herein, subject to the amendments and modification contained in this article. A copy of the manual shall be maintained at the offices of the director or his designee and open for public inspection. Any conflicts between the provisions of this article and the manual shall be resolved in favor of the manual. References to state personnel, agencies, and fees shall be interpreted, where required, as meaning the City of Stone Mountain municipal equivalents.
(Ord. No. 2015-15, Pt. I(§ 25.19), 6-2-15)
1277:
Unless specifically set forth in the permit, no utility may occupy the city right-of-way unless sufficient space is available so that the free flow and safety of traffic and other capacity considerations are not unduly impaired and the installation does not prevent the department from reasonably maintaining the streets, structures, traffic control devices and other appurtenant facilities, and further provided that maintenance and operations of the facilities do not jeopardize the traffic, street structure, other users of the right-of-way or the right-of-way itself.
(Ord. No. 2015-15, Pt. I(§ 25.20), 6-2-15)
1278:
If the grades or lines of any street within the city right-of-way are changed at any time by the city during the term of the permit and this change involves an area in which the utility's facilities are located, then the utility shall, at its own cost and expense and upon the request of the city upon reasonable notice, protect or promptly alter or relocate the facilities, or any part thereof, so as to conform with such new grades or lines. In the event the utility refuses or neglects to so protect, alter, or relocate all or part of the facilities, the city shall have the right to break through, remove, alter, or relocate all or any part of the facilities without any liability to the utility and the utility shall pay to the city the costs incurred in connection with such breaking through, removal, alteration, or relocation.
(Ord. No. 2015-15, Pt. I(§ 25.21), 6-2-15)
1279:
Unless otherwise provided in a valid service agreement, no placement of any pole or wireholding structure of the utility is to be considered a vested interest in the right-of-way, and such poles or structures are to be removed, relocated underground, or modified by the utility at its own expense whenever the city determines that the public convenience would be enhanced thereby. The facilities shall be so located and installed as to cause minimum interference with the rights and convenience of property owners.
(Ord. No. 2015-15, Pt. I(§ 25.22), 6-2-15)
1280:
As provided in O.C.G.A § 25-9-6 (the Georgia Utility Facility Protection Act) and other applicable state law currently in place or as amended, no utility shall commence, perform, or engage in blasting or in excavating with mechanized excavating facilities unless and until the utility planning the blasting or excavating has given forty-eight (48) hours' notice by submitting a locate request to the utility protection center, beginning the next working day after such notice is provided, excluding hours during days other than working days.
(Ord. No. 2015-15, Pt. I(§ 25.23), 6-2-15)
1281:
Each utility shall be responsible for the cost of repairing any facilities in the rights-of-way and adjoining property or other facilities which it or its facilities damage.
(Ord. No. 2015-15, Pt. I(§ 25.24), 6-2-15)

1308:
This chapter shall be known and may be cited as "The Land Subdivision Regulations of the City of Stone Mountain, Georgia."
(Code 1976, § 8-2001)
1309:
For the purposes of this chapter, words and terms used herein are defined as follows:
Alley means a street which affords only secondary means of access to abutting property, and not intended for general traffic.
Block means a track of land bounded by streets, or by a combination of streets and public parks, cemeteries, railroad rights-of-way, shorelines of waterways, or boundary lines of municipalities or counties.
Building means a structure having a roof supported by columns or walls, for the housing or shelter of persons, animals or goods. Where roofed structures are separated from each other by party walls having no opening for passage, each portion so separated shall be considered a separate building.
Building height means the vertical distance measured from the average elevation of the proposed finished grade of the lot at the front of the building to the highest point of the coping of a flat roof, to the average height level between eaves and ridge of gable, hip, and gambrel roofs, and to the deck line in the case of a mansard roof.
Building official means the authorized building inspector for the city.
Building line (setback) means the line established by law past which a building shall not exceed as determined by front, side, and rear yards herein.
Building permit means a written permit issued by the building inspector authorizing construction, renovation, or repairs to a structure.
Building, principal, means a building in which is conducted the predominant use of the lot on which it is situated.
City means the City of Stone Mountain, Georgia.
City council means the mayor and city council of the City of Stone Mountain.
City engineer means the city engineer of the City of Stone Mountain or person designated by the city council to serve in this capacity.
Condominium means the ownership in fee simple title of a single unit in a multi-unit structure and undivided ownership, in common with other purchases, of the common elements of the structure and including the land and its appurtenances.
Construction plans means the maps or drawings accompanying a subdivision plat and showing the specific location and design of the improvements to be installed in the subdivision in accordance with the requirements of the design standards of this chapter as a condition of the approval of the plat.
Cul-de-sac means a street having one (1) end open to traffic, the other end being permanently terminated by a vehicular turn-around.
Double frontage lot means a lot having frontage on two (2) streets, as distinguished from a corner lot.
Drainage easement means an area set aside for the purpose of transporting stormwater. Maintenance of these easements are the responsibility of the private property owner.
Driveway means an accessway connecting one (1) or more dwelling units and/or their parking spaces with a street.
Easement means a grant by a property owner of the use of land for a specific purpose or purposes by the general public, a corporation, or a certain person or persons in a county.
Engineer means a registered, professional engineer, licensed by the state.
Grading means any land-disturbing activity including clearing and grubbing, stripping, cutting, filling, stockpiling, or any combination thereof, and shall include the land in its cut or filled condition.
Improvements guarantee means a guarantee in the form of a bond or certified check to insure completion of required subdivision paving improvements.
Health department means the county health department which is duly authorized to perform health services in the county.
Land use plan means a development plan or any part thereof adopted by the city council which indicates the general location for the various physical classes of public works, places, and structures and depicting the general planned physical development of the city.
Large lot (estate) subdivision means a subdivision consisting of ten (10) or more lots or building sites for the purpose of constructing single-family residential structures. All lots included as part of such subdivisions shall be a minimum of 1.75 acres in land area.
Lot means a parcel of land occupied or intended for occupancy by one principal building or use, and any accessory building and use incidental to it. In determining the area and dimensions of a lot, no portion of the right-of-way of a street or crosswalk may be included.
Lot area means the computed ground area inside the lot lines.
Lot, corner, means a lot abutting on two (2) or more streets at their intersection.
Lot coverage means the computed ground area occupied by all buildings within a lot.
Lot depth means the mean horizontal distance between the front and rear lines.
Lot, interior, means a lot other than a corner lot or double frontage lot.
Lot width means the distance between side lot lines measured at the minimum front yard setback line.
Nonresidential subdivision means a subdivision whose intended use is other than residential, such as commercial or industrial. Such subdivision shall comply with the applicable provisions of this chapter.
Owner means any individual, firm, association, syndicate, partnership, corporation, trust or any other legal entity having sufficient (fifty-one (51) percent) proprietary interest in the land sought to be subdivided to commence and maintain proceedings to subdivide the same under this chapter.
Parcel means a general term including all plots of land shown with separate identification on the official tax appraisal maps.
Person includes individuals, firms, partnerships, corporations, associations, organizations, trusts, companies, governmental bodies and all other legal entities.
Planning commission means the Stone Mountain Planning Commission.
Plat, final, means the map or plan of record for subdivision and any accompanying material, as required in this chapter.
Plat, preliminary, means the preliminary drawing or drawings, described in this chapter, indicating the proposed manner or layout of the subdivision to be submitted to the planning commission for approval.
Public improvement means any drainage ditch, roadway, parkway, sidewalk, pedestrianway, tree, lawn, off-street parking area, lot improvement or other facility for which the city may ultimately assume the responsibility for maintenance and operation, or which may affect an improvement for which city responsibility is established.
Public street means a street over which the general public has acquired the right of use.
Public utilities means water, gas, sanitary and storm sewer, electrical and communications lines and facilities.
Resubdivision means a change in a map of an approved or recorded subdivision plat if such change affects any street layout on such map or area reserved thereon for public use, or any lot line.
Right-of-way means a strip of land occupied or intended to be occupied by any or all of the following: a street, crosswalk, railroad, road, electric transmission line, oil or gas pipeline, water main, sanitary or storm sewer main, shade trees or other special use.
Right-of-way width means the distance between property lines measured at right angles to the centerline of the street.
Shoulder means that portion of a street or road from the outer edge of the paved surface or back of curb to the inside edge of the ditch or gutter or original ground surface.
Sidewalk means the portion of the right-of-way which is parallel to the street or road which is intended for pedestrian traffic.
Sketch plan means a generalized sketch of the proposed subdivision submitted prior to the preparation of the preliminary plat to enable the subdivider to reach general agreement with the city planner and city engineer as to the form of the plat and the objectives of this chapter.
Street means a right-of-way for vehicular traffic whether designated as street, highway, thoroughfare, parkway, expressway, freeway, road, avenue, drive, expressway, freeway, boulevard, lane, place, circle, or otherwise (see also the definition for public way, private street, private access drive, and right-of-way). Various classifications of streets may be defined as follows:
(1) Arterial. A street which is used primarily for fast and heavy traffic flow; is of considerable continuity; and is used as a traffic artery for intercommunication among large areas.
(2) Major collector. A street which carries traffic from activity centers and minor collector streets to arterial streets and streets of higher classification.
(3) Minor collector. Principal entrance streets to subdivisions and the main streets for circulation within a subdivision which serve a network of four (4) or more local streets. Minor collector streets are designed so that traffic circulation in a subdivision would cause such a street to be used as link between local streets and major collector or arterial streets.
(4) Local. A street used primarily for access to abutting properties as opposed to the collection and dispersion of traffic.
(5) Cul-de-sac. A local street which is parallel to, and adjacent to an arterial street or highway and which provides access to abutting properties and protection from through traffic.
(6) Marginal access. A street which is parallel to, and adjacent to an arterial street or highway and which provides access to abutting properties and protection from through traffic.
Street grade means the grade of the centerline of a street measured at any point along the street expressed as a percent.
Street, city, means a street which is owned or maintained by the city.
Street, county. A street which is owned or maintained by the county.
Structure means anything constructed or erected, the use of which requires a location on the ground, or attached to something having a location on the ground. Among other things structure includes buildings, fences, signs, swimming pools, etc.
Subdivider means any person dividing or proposing to divide land so as to constitute a subdivision, including any agent of the subdivider.
Subdivision means any land, which is divided or proposed to be divided into two (2) or more lots or parcels. The following are not included within this definition:
(1) The combination or recombination of portions of previously platted lots where the total number of lots is not increased and the resultant lots are equal to the standards of this chapter.
(2) The division of land into parcels of five (5) acres or more where no new street is involved.
Surveyor means a registered, practicing surveyor, licensed by the state.
Zoning enforcement officer means that person appointed by the mayor and city council to enforce provisions of the zoning ordinance and this chapter.
Zoning ordinance means the zoning ordinance of the city (Appendix A of this Code).
(Ord. of 8-4-87)
Cross reference— Zoning, App. A.

(a) In the interest of orderly, planned, and efficient development and furtherance of the general health, safety and welfare of the city and its citizens it is hereby declared to be the policy of the city to consider the subdivision of land and its development to be subject to the control of the city in order to ensure consistency with the adopted land use plan.

1320:
(a) Generally. Whenever any residential or nonresidential subdivision of land is proposed, and prior to issuing any permit for erection of a structure in such proposed subdivision, the owner, subdivider, or authorized agent shall apply for, and secure approval of such proposed subdivision in accordance with the following procedure, which includes four (4) steps.
(1) Sketch plan.
(2) Preliminary plat.
(3) Construction plans.
(4) Final plat.
All submittals shall be consistent with provisions of the zoning ordinance and other codes, ordinances and regulations of the city.
(b) Subdivision review procedure. The following procedures shall be followed when submitting plats:
(1) The subdivider and his professional representative shall meet with the secretary of the planning commission to review the sketch plan.
(2) No later than fifteen (15) days prior to the meeting date of the planning commission the subdivider shall submit three (3) copies of a preliminary plat to the secretary of the planning commission for review and local distribution, and appropriate fees shall be paid.
(3) The subdivider shall also deliver one (1) copy of the preliminary plat to the following city and county departments for review:
a. Water department.
b. Health department.
c. Water pollution control department (if subdivision is to be served by a community sewer system).
d. Board of education.
e. Fire marshal.
(4) The secretary of the planning commission and city engineer shall utilize the fifteen-day period to the planning commission meeting date to review the preliminary plat. The subdivider shall be notified if any changes are necessary to achieve compliance with this chapter and shall be responsible for having all changes made and a revised plat submitted prior to the planning commission meeting date. The subdivider shall also bring evidence of approval of those departments listed in paragraph (3) above to the planning commission meeting.
(5) At the hearing, the planning commission shall approve, approve subject to modifications, table, or disapprove the preliminary plat. If approval is given subject to modifications, the required modifications shall be provided to the subdivider in writing, and all modifications shall be made and approved by the secretary of the planning commission and city engineer prior to issuance of a grading permit. If the preliminary plat is disapproved, the planning commission shall notify the subdivider in writing, citing the reasons for disapproval. The action of the planning commission shall be noted on the original of the preliminary plat, and one (1) copy shall be returned to the subdivider.
(6) Preliminary plat approval is tentative, pending submission of a final plat, and is valid for a period not to exceed twelve (12) months, after which it shall expire.
(7) A grading permit shall be issued only subsequent to approval of construction plans.
(8) Prior to installation of any improvements and before submittal of a final plat, two (2) copies of construction plans depicting the design of all required improvements shall be submitted to the city for review by the city engineer.
(9) Within twelve (12) months from the date of preliminary plat approval, five (5) copies of a final plat for one (1) or more phases of the subdivision shall be submitted to the secretary of the planning commission at least fifteen (15) days prior to the date of the meeting of the planning commission and all appropriate fees paid. The subdivider shall also provide satisfactory evidence of improvements installation or provide the necessary improvements guarantee. Failure to submit within this time period shall void the plat unless an extension for a period not to exceed six (6) months is granted by the planning commission. Such extension must be applied for in writing by the subdivider.
(10) The planning commission at the hearing shall determine whether all requirements of this chapter have been met and either approve, table, or disapprove the final plat. If the final plat is disapproved, the planning commission shall notify the subdivider in writing, citing the reasons for disapproval.
(11) When all improvements required by this chapter have been made, the subdivider shall provide to the city engineer one (1) complete set of as-built drawings depicting the subdivision and all improvements. A letter from the subdivider's registered professional engineer shall accompany this submittal and certify that all improvements have been installed in accordance with the construction plans previously submitted to, and approved by the city engineer.
(12) The approved final plat is to be recorded in the office of the clerk of superior court of the county within sixty (60) days of the date of final plat approval.
(c) Fees to recover the costs of review for the preliminary plat, construction plans and final plat shall be set by resolution of the mayor and city council.
(Ord. of 8-4-87; Ord. No. 07-06, pt. I, 6-5-07)
1321:
For any change in a plat of an approved or recorded subdivision plat, if such change affects any street layout shown on such plat, or area reserved thereon for public use, or any lot line, or if it affects any plat or plan legally reached prior to the adoption of any regulations controlling subdivisions, such change shall be submitted to the building official for review by the building official and city engineer. 1322:

1323:
(a) Duty of subdivider. Whenever the subdivision of a tract of land within the city is proposed, the subdivider or his agent shall consult early and informally with the secretary of the planning commission. The subdivider may submit sketch plans and data showing existing conditions within the site and in its vicinity and the proposed layout and development of the subdivision.
(b) Purpose of review. The purpose of the preapplication review is to facilitate the subsequent preparation of plans.
(c) Fees. No fees shall be charged for a preapplication review.
(d) Sketch plan specifications. The sketch plan shall represent the entire area which the subdivider contemplates developing, including those units/sections not scheduled for immediate development. The sketch plan submitted shall be prepared in ink or pencil on a reproducible medium and can be a freehand rendering. The sketch plan shall illustrate the ultimate development of the entire parcel(s) for which formal plat approval will initially be requested. Three (3) copies of the sketch plan shall be submitted. It shall be prepared at a scale of not more than one (1) inch equals one hundred (100) feet and is to include site topography at a contour interval of ten (10) feet or less. The sketch plan shall include at minimum the following information:
(1) Subdivision name and unit if within existing subdivision.
(2) Proposed name if not within a previously platted subdivision.
(3) Name, address and telephone number of legal owner or agent of the property.
(4) Name, address and telephone number of registered professionals responsible for subdivision design, for design of improvements, and for surveys.
(5) Date, scale, and north arrow.
(6) Vicinity map.
(7) Proposed use of property to be subdivided.
(8) Total acreage.
(9) Location of existing property lines, major easements/rights-of-way, watercourses, drainage areas and ditches, and distinctive natural features.
(10) The location and width of all existing or proposed streets or public ways within; or directly adjacent to the subject property.
(11) Existing buildings.
(12) The approximate location and width of proposed streets.
(13) The approximate location of all proposed or existing lots and the square footage of the smallest lot.
(14) The location of flood hazard areas taken from the HUD (FEMA) maps.
(15) Statement of proposed water and/or sewer supply or collection method.
(16) Zoning of subject property and adjacent properties.
(Code 1976, § 2-1; Ord. of 8-4-87)
1324:

(1) A letter requesting review and approval of a preliminary plat and giving the name and address of the person to whom the notice of the hearing by the planning commission on the preliminary plat shall be sent;
(2) The preliminary plat and other documents, as specified in section 26-42.
(Code 1976, § 8-2005)
1325:
(a) Report, hearing required. The secretary of the planning commission shall check the plat submitted pursuant to section 26-40 for conformance to the rules and regulations of this chapter and report his findings and recommendations to the planning commission, which shall afford a hearing on the preliminary plat, notice of the time and place of which shall be sent by the secretary of the planning commission by registered or certified mail to the persons designated in the letter requesting preliminary plat review and approval, not less than five (5) days prior to the date of the hearing.
(b) Action by planning commission. Thereafter, the planning commission shall give tentative approval or disapproval to the preliminary plat. A notation of the action shall be made on two (2) copies of the preliminary plat, including a statement of the reasons therefor if the preliminary plat is disapproved. One (1) copy shall be returned to the subdivider or his agent and one (1) copy added to the records of the planning commission.
(c) Effect, duration of approval. Tentative approval of a preliminary plat does not constitute approval of a final plat. It indicates only approval of the layout as a guide to the preparation of the final plat. Tentative approval shall expire and be null and void after a period of one (1) year unless an extension of time is approved by the planning commission.
(Code 1976, § 8-2006)
1326:
(a) Scale. The preliminary plat shall be clearly and legibly drawn at a scale not smaller than one hundred (100) feet to one (1) inch.
(b) Sheet size. Sheet size shall be twenty-three (23) inches by twenty-eight (28) inches. If the complete plat cannot be shown on one (1) sheet of this size, it may be shown on more than one (1) sheet with an index map on a separate sheet of the same size.
(c) Ground elevations. The preliminary plat shall show ground elevations, based on a datum plane approved by the secretary of the planning commission, by contours at an interval of not more than five (5) feet where the ground slope is regular or at an interval of not more than two (2) feet where necessary because of irregular land.
(d) Preliminary plat content. The preliminary plat shall represent the entire area which the subdivider contemplates developing, including possible unit divisions not scheduled for immediate development. Copies of the preliminary plat shall be submitted for review and copies shall be transmitted by the subdivider to the appropriate city and county agencies. The preliminary plat shall be prepared by a licensed land surveyor or registered professional engineer. The preliminary plat shall be prepared in ink on a reproducible medium. The submittal copies shall consist of black-line or blue-line prints on a white background, and the submittal shall include such other documents as necessary to meet the requirements of this chapter. If the preliminary plat is prepared by a registered professional engineer reference must be made to the legal survey of the parcel. A copy of the survey must be included with the preliminary plat if not stamped by a licensed land surveyor. The preliminary plat shall contain the following information:
(1) Name of subdivision.
(2) Names and right-of-way width of all proposed streets.
(3) The name and address and telephone number of the owner or owners of the land to be subdivided and the name, address and telephone number of the subdivider.
(4) The seal(s), name(s), and addresses of the licensed land surveyor or registered professional engineer.
(5) Date, graphic scale, numeric scale, north arrow and space for revisions.
(6) Vicinity map indicating streets and highways, railroads and other significant features within; or adjacent to the proposed subdivision.
(7) Proposed use of property to be subdivided.
(8) Total acreage, outlet acreage if applicable and the acreage of the smallest lot.
(9) Present zoning of subject property and adjacent properties.
(10) The location of property with respect to surrounding streets, and the names of adjoining developments.
(11) The location and dimensions of all boundary lines of the property, to be expressed in feet.
(12) Unit divisions if known, or staged development if proposed by the subdivider.
(13) The approximate location and sizes of existing sewers, water mains, drainage or other underground structures within, and immediately adjacent to the subject property.
(14) The location of existing and proposed streets, easements, water bodies, flood hazard areas and floodplains, streams, and other pertinent features such as swamps, railroads, buildings, parks, cemeteries, drainage ditches, bridges and rock outcrops.
(15) The location and width of proposed streets.
(16) Reference points from proposed intersections to permanent features.
(17) The location and scaled dimensions of all proposed or existing lots. The minimum front yard setback on all lots and side lot setback for corner lots.
(18) The location and scaled dimensions and acreage of all property proposed to be set aside for park or playground use, or other public or private reservation, with designation of the purpose thereof, and conditions, if any, of the dedication or reservation.
(19) Sufficient data acceptable to the city engineer to determine readily the location, bearing, and length of all property lines, and to reproduce such lines upon the ground; and the location of all proposed monuments. Control survey must close and balance within a tolerance of one (1) foot in ten thousand (10,000) feet.
(20) Blocks shall be lettered in alphabetical order. The blocks in numbered additions to subdivisions bearing the same name shall be lettered consecutively throughout the several additions.
(21) All lots in each block shall be consecutively numbered. Outlots shall be numbered in a logical sequence.
(22) List of proposed utilities to be located underground.
(23) A statement of the proposed method of water supply, major drainage provisions, detention areas, and proposed sewerage disposal plans. If the development is to utilize private sewer, all information required by the health department shall be provided.
(24) The total number of units if not a single-family subdivision.
(25) Certification for signature of the chairman of the planning commission approving the preliminary plat.
The lack of information under any item specified herein, or improper information supplied by the applicant, shall be cause of disapproval of a preliminary plat.
(e) Certificate of tentative approval. A certificate of tentative approval of the preliminary plat by the planning commission shall be inscribed on the plat as follows:

1344:
(a) Generally. Development of subdivisions is to be accomplished with minimal earth moving and disruption to the natural topography of the site. It is the intent of this chapter that existing or manmade slopes be modified or designed in such a way as to minimize potential for erosion and to maximize ease of maintenance. Subdivision development shall conform to provisions of the erosion and sedimentation control chapter of this Code.
(b) Slope design standards. The following design standards for slopes will be adhered to:
(1) No existing or proposed cut or fill slope shall exceed three (3) horizontal units to one (1) vertical unit within eleven (11) feet of the edge of pavement or back of curb. Beyond such eleven (11) feet the slope may be greater than three (3) to one (1) up to a maximum slope of one and one-half (1½) horizontal units to one (1) vertical unit, provided that all cut and fill shall be within the prescribed right-of-way of the road or slope easements. All grading as provided within this section shall be completed and approved by the city engineer prior to the installation of any utilities.
(2) All fill slopes created for the purpose of street construction shall have a compaction of not less than ninety-five (95) percent as determined by established engineering practices.
(3) Slopes flatter than those set forth in the foregoing paragraphs may be required, when, in the opinion of the city engineer, the general nature of the soil involved warrants a flatter slope. To control surface drainage on existing and proposed slopes, berm ditches may be required at the top and at the intersection of the slope and ground line.
(4) All slopes created or existing within the subdivision or as a result of the subdivision development shall be planted or otherwise protected from erosion and failure. Such planting and other protection from erosion and failure shall be completed and shall be undertaken immediately upon creation of any slope steeper than two (2) horizontal feet to one (1) vertical foot and completed without delay in accordance with plans and specifications approved by the city engineer. In addition, the subdivider may be required to provide a fence, hedge, guardrail or other protective device, specified by the city engineer along ridges in excess of twenty (20) vertical feet in height and with slopes in excess of 1.5:1 (horizontal:vertical) to prevent dangerous falls for children and other residents of the subdivision. At the option of the city engineer the developer shall provide certified test results of compaction and any materials provided at the location and frequency determined necessary by the city engineer.
(Ord. of 8-4-87)
Cross reference— Erosion and sediment control, Ch. 9.
1345:
(a) The storm water drainage system and easements shall be separate and independent of any sanitary sewer system and easement.
(b) Storm water runoff and storm sewer or channel design shall be designed by a method as approved by the city engineer, and a copy of design computations shall be submitted along with the construction plans. Inlets shall be provided so that surface water is not carried for a distance of more than six hundred (600) feet in the gutter. When calculations indicate that curb capacities are exceeded at a point, no further allowance shall be made for flow beyond that point, and basins shall be used to intercept flow at that point.
(c) Natural drainage channels existing within a subdivision shall be improved by the subdivider to specifications approved by the city engineer if erosion, flooding, or hazard will be created by the continued existence thereof, as determined by the city engineer.
(1) Accessibility to public storm sewers. Where a public storm sewer is accessible, the applicant shall install storm sewer facilities, or if no outlets are within a reasonable distance, adequate provision shall be made for the disposal of storm waters, subject to the specifications of the city engineer. If a connection to a public storm sewer will be provided eventually, as determined by the city engineer and the planning commission, the developer shall make arrangements for future storm water disposal by public utility system at the time the plat receives final approval.
(2) Accommodation of upstream drainage areas. A culvert or other drainage facility shall in each case be large enough to accommodate potential runoff from its entire upstream drainage area whether inside or outside the subdivision. The city engineer shall approve the necessary size of the facility which has been designed by a registered professional engineer, based on one hundred ten (110) percent of the current storm runoff for the one-hundred-year storm for culverts under streets, and the twenty-five-year storm for all other culverts. Minimum pipe size shall be eighteen (18) inches.
(3) Effect on downstream drainage areas. The developer shall study and the city engineer shall review and approve the effect of each subdivision on existing downstream drainage facilities outside the area of the subdivision. Drainage studies together with such other studies as shall be appropriate, shall serve as a guide to needed improvements. Where it is anticipated that the additional runoff incident to the development of the subdivision will overload an existing downstream drainage facility, the planning commission may withhold approval of the subdivision until provision has been made for the improvement of the potential condition in such sum as the planning commission shall determine. No subdivision shall be approved unless adequate drainage will be provided to an adequate watercourse or facility.
(4) Drainage easements. Where topography or other conditions are such as to make impractical the inclusion of drainage facilities within road rights-of-way, perpetual unobstructed easements at least twenty (20) feet in width for such drainage facilities shall be provided across property outside the road lines and with satisfactory access to the road. Where pipe size warrants, a ten-foot easement shall be permitted. Easements shall be indicated on the plat. Drainage easements shall be carried from the road to a natural watercourse or to other drainage facilities. Easements less than twenty (20) feet may be approved by the city manager. Low-lying land along watercourses subject to flooding or overflowing during storm periods, whether or not included in areas for dedication, shall be preserved and retained in their natural state as drainageways.
(Ord. of 8-4-87)
Cross reference— Sewers, Ch. 22.

1348:
(a) Generally. Applicants are required to locate all utility facilities underground throughout the subdivision. All existing and proposed utility easements outside of road rights-of-way shall be shown on the construction plans and final plats.
(b) Location. Overhead utility lines shall be located along the front, side and/or rear of property lines, or at such other locations as may be approved by the utility companies involved.
(1) The facilities for underground utilities or conduits for their construction shall be in place prior to final surfacing of streets.
(2) All facilities for utilities shall, where possible be placed in easements provided for that purpose in the subdivision or located as approved by the city engineer.
(3) No subdivision street shall be cut for underground utilities.
(c) Easements. Utility easements for electric and telephone service lines, sewage lines, water lines or other such utilities located along rear lot lines or side lot lines or, passing through a lot shall be at least ten (10) feet wide, five (5) feet on each lot, and more if determined by the city engineer.
(d) Road surfacing and improvements. After utilities have been installed, the applicant shall construct concrete curbs and gutters and shall surface or cause to be surfaced, roadways to the widths prescribed in this chapter. Such surfacing shall be of such character as is suitable for the expected traffic and in harmony with similar improvements in the surrounding area. Adequate provision shall be made for culverts, drains, and bridges.
(1) For residential streets, base and paving shall be one (1) of the following types:
Type I: Six-inch crusher run stone base applied on a properly prepared sub-grade brought to a ninety-five (95) percent compaction (Standard Proctor). A two-inch plant mix asphalt Type E or F is to be applied to the base.
Type II: Five-inch compacted crusher run stone base applied on a properly prepared sub-grade brought to a ninety-five (95) percent compaction (Standard Proctor). A two-inch plant mix asphalt (Asphaltic Base Type B) is to be applied to the base which meets with state approved standards for plant mix asphalt. A one-and-one-half-inch plant mix asphalt Type E or F shall be applied over the binder.
(2) For commercial streets, base and paving shall be as follows:
Type III: Six-inch crusher run stone base applied on a properly prepared sub-grade brought to a ninety-five (95) percent compaction (Standard Proctor). A two-and-one-half-inch asphaltic base Type B covered by a two-and-one-half-inch surface course Type E or F plant mix asphalt.
(3) For industrial streets, base and paving shall be as follows:
Type IV: Eight-inch crusher run stone base applied on a properly prepared sub-grade brought to a ninety-five (95) percent compaction (Standard Proctor). A three-inch asphaltic base Type B covered by a one-and-one-half-inch surface course of Type E or F plant mix asphalt.
(4) Concrete curbs and gutters shall be constructed with three thousand (3,000) pounds per square inch at twenty-eight-day breaking strength, twelve (12) inches by thirty (30) inches. Roll type curb and gutter shall not be permitted in single-family subdivisions.
(5) Primary highway systems. Whenever a proposed subdivision abuts an arterial road or major collector, an access road or lane with curbing extending the full length of the subdivision along such highway and providing limited access thereto may be required at a distance suitable for the use of the land between such access road or lane and highway.
(6) Driveways. Driveways shall have a slope of not more than a positive or negative twelve (12) percent for a distance of ten (10) feet measured along the driveway centerline from the right-of-way line. Centerline elevations on all driveways, at the right-of-way line, must be a minimum of six (6) inches above the elevation of the gutter line.
(Ord. of 8-4-87)
